transformNotes: Rows of ECDICT ecdict.csv whose 'tag' column contains cet4 / cet6 respectively; one word pack per level. 'meanings' comes from splitting the source 'translation' cell on newlines (a literal backslash-n in a few rows is treated as a newline too). A leading part-of-speech marker (n. / v. / vt. / vi. / a. / adv. ...) is removed from the meaning text and recorded in 'partOfSpeech' only when the whole entry uses exactly one distinct marker; entries with mixed markers keep their text verbatim, marker included. 'phonetic' is the source 'phonetic' column with one leading and trailing slash added when absent; ECDICT carries a single transcription, so phoneticUs and phoneticUk are empty strings and 'phonetic' holds that single value. ECDICT has no example sentences, no collocations and no separate US/UK phonetics, so those fields are empty rather than invented. Rows with an empty word or an empty translation were dropped; case-insensitive duplicates inside one list kept the richest row. 'id' is level + 1-based index in the emitted order.

replaced.U+0454 CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER UKRAINIAN I: U+025B LATIN SMALL LETTER OPEN E

phoneticNormalization.note: Pure notation transliteration of the source's Kingsoft-style phonetics; no pronunciation was added, changed or invented.
